The iPhone 18 Pro is set to launch soon, and rumors suggest the Pro Max model may have unique advantages in one or two key areas this year. Here's what to expect.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max will see a bigger battery life boost this year, and may also have camera advantages

For many years, Apple's Pro models launched each year have stayed largely the same in terms of features.

Beyond the Pro Max's clearly larger display and longer battery life advantages, it has occasionally had an exclusive camera feature.

This year for the iPhone 18 Pro, rumors suggest Apple will continue with this strategy.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery life has always been expected to last longer than the iPhone 18 Pro. But based on details recently leaked from regulatory filings, the situation appears more pronounced than usual.

Here's a rumored spec comparison of battery capacity between the new and old models (eSIM versions):

  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: 5567mAh
  • iPhone 18 Pro: 4288mAh
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max: 5088mAh
  • iPhone 17 Pro: 4252mAh

As seen above, the iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery capacity is roughly 10% larger than the previous generation. As for the iPhone 18 Pro, its battery capacity is nearly identical to the iPhone 17 Pro.

Both new models will benefit from efficiency gains in the A20 Pro chip and the C2 modem, leading to improved battery life. But if you're still weighing which to choose, the iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery life advantage will be more pronounced than ever.

One cost of the larger battery is that the device will also be heavier compared to the iPhone 18 Pro.

Another potential difference lies in the camera. Of course we'd expect both Pro models to have the same feature set, but last fall a reliable leaker mentioned that an upcoming variable aperture system might be exclusive to the Pro Max.

No other source has confirmed this yet. However, Mark Gurman has said this year will be a particularly big year for camera upgrades, so Apple could indeed be saving at least one improvement for the larger, more expensive model.

Are you a Pro or Pro Max user? What differentiating features would make you switch? Let us know in the comments.
